statements.status_notes: Passing an effectively empty string to the ",ccs=" syntax extension of the mode argument in the fopen function in the GNU C Library version 2.45 or earlier may result in a heap buffer overflow when the mode string input to the function is attacker controlled. This usage pattern is not seen in applications in common GNU/Linux distributions.
statements.impact_statement: This heap buffer overflow requires an application to call glibc's fopen function with an attacker-controlled mode string containing an effectively empty ",ccs=" syntax extension. Liquibase Secure's runtime never constructs fopen mode strings from external input; the JVM's own file I/O does not use this glibc idiom.

statements.status_notes: Calling strfmon and strfmon_l in the GNU C Library version 2.38 to 2.44 can write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer when a conversion uses right-justified width padding. At the time of publication, no network-facing application impact is known.
statements.impact_statement: This glibc flaw is reachable only through application calls to strfmon or strfmon_l with a vulnerable right-justified width-padding pattern. The Liquibase Secure image inherits the OS package from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (`docker/Dockerfile:2`) and the container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles, entrypoint scripts, and application source found no references to strfmon or strfmon_l, so the vulnerable API path is not reachable from the stock Liquibase Secure runtime.

statements.status_notes: Calling tdelete on a sufficiently deep tree in the GNU C Library version 2.1 to 2.44 may write one pointer past the end of an alloca-allocated array on the stack, which may crash the application. No affected application in common distributions has been identified.
statements.impact_statement: This glibc flaw requires an application to use tsearch/tdelete on a very deep tree. The Liquibase Secure image inherits the OS package from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (`docker/Dockerfile:2`) and the container entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI (`docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8`, `docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:119`). A focused grep across the runtime Dockerfiles, entrypoint scripts, and application source found no references to tsearch or tdelete, so the vulnerable API path is not reachable from the stock Liquibase Secure runtime.

statements.status_notes: The iconv() function in the GNU C Library versions 2.43 and earlier may crash due to an assertion failure when converting inputs from the IBM1390 or IBM1399 character sets, which may be used to remotely crash an application. This vulnerability can be trivially mitigated by removing the IBM1390 and IBM1399 character sets from systems that do not need them.
statements.impact_statement: The scanned image reports libc-bin 2.39-0ubuntu8.7, below Ubuntu's fixed 2.39-0ubuntu8.8, but this issue requires an application to process IBM1390 or IBM1399 encoded input through glibc's iconv conversion path. The stock Liquibase Secure runtime is the Liquibase Java CLI, and a review of its build and runtime path found no references to iconv or those IBM1390 or IBM1399 code pages.

statements.status_notes: Calling wordexp with WRDE_APPEND in the GNU C Library version 2.0 to version 2.43 can cause the interface to return invalid memory in the we_wordv member, which on subsequent calls to wordfree may abort the process.
statements.impact_statement: This flaw requires an application to call glibc's wordexp function with the WRDE_APPEND flag. Neither the JVM nor the container's bash entrypoint calls wordexp; this is a C-language shell-word-expansion API that Liquibase Secure's Java and bash-only runtime path never invokes.
